system.summary: One-part Polish syllabary-nomenclator of about 2,200 dotted number groups in alphabetical order (two runs), with a null band 1775-1788.
system.notes: Second alphabetical run from about 1870; letters under groups mark variants; a framed 4000/9933 second table in two December letters is not read.

prior_solution.where: Clear texts of 103 of the 106 despatches in AGAD ZbPop 419 and 417 (fair copies or the cabinet's decipherments, signed Deboli, with reception notes); used by Łojek 1962 and Rolnik 2025

conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue task page; no other input.

solution.what: AGAD letter lists (ZbPop17.xml, 419, 417, 420, 4) and scans on agadd2; key units 444/451/453/454 not online.
Zielińska & Danilczyk Deboli 1782 introduction (cabinet decipherments in AKP 265), Rolnik 2025, web search: no decipherment of ZbPop 17 itself.
Clear series ZbPop 419 as the plaintext: dates pair for 100 of 106 cipher despatches.
6 Jan 1789 cipher (760 groups) and its clear text transcribed.
Hand alignment of the closing paragraph: lokacya = 623 461 2150 twice, aby = 1900 three times, warunkami/warunkow.
One-part syllabary in alphabetical order, second run from about 1870.
align.py: DP alignment of cipher groups to 0-10 clear letters with an alphabetical-order cost and iterated anchors; 1, 3, 8, then 11 pairs (630 anchors).
Groups 1775-1788 align to nothing (1786: 93 of 94): a null band.
LM gap-filling inside alphabetical brackets on the held-out 18 Dec letter: 5-8 of 171 hidden groups exact; dropped.
Key from 7 pairs, 18 Dec decoded blind: 95.6% of groups valued, 91.4% of decoded letters in the order of the real clear text.
Clear texts of 22, 25, 29 Dec found misfiled in ZbPop 417 (catalogued 1788).

Hand reading of the three despatches without a clear text (read.py, reading/*.fix.tsv): 25 Mar 95.5%, 14 Dec 89.4%, 10 May 84.8% of groups read as sense; groups whose key value does not fit marked unread.
deboli1791's independent code tables for the same code tried on every unread group: agree with this key, three readings added; its code B absent.
Framed 4000 9933 runs (22, 29 Dec) hold French passages in a separate table: the aligner places the French phrases of the clear copies exactly inside them.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 5056 tokens, 759 types, pl-1790 order 4: reading -2.329 per letter; random keys -3.084 (z 11.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.307 (mean -2.322, z -0.6); annealer on the real text -2.296. Verdict: underdetermined.

Decrypt audit (research/decrypt_audit): key_pass.tsv applied to the fifteen transcriptions; 3,704 of 13,121 compared words depart. Twelve texts are compared with the archive's clear copies, not with a reading made here: the figure there measures the aligner's table (commonest aligned string per group; 81% of 22,171 aligned groups equal the key value in place, 9% a longer or shorter form, 9% different). c042 and c104: the folio label at the head of each line ('k.138r.01:') was read as text; rebuilt from key_pass.tsv, fix.tsv and the transcriptions with read.py's rules, both decoded files and the three reading tsv files come out identical, the remaining departures being groups marked unread by hand, '?' groups, base-group fallbacks and bracketed context readings. c024 worded reading: 14 word endings taken from the key's alternatives column and 5 places with letters supplied without a mark (odprawie, iest, powiedzieć, przyszło że się, a second 'na'). No file changed.

Marked the unmarked departures of the 25 March worded reading (reading/c024_1789-03-25.txt): 18 words with [ ] round letters the key's main value does not give (WKMc[i] x7, Rossy[i] x2, list[u], ie[st], sie[bie], [od]prawi[e], pow[ie]dzieć, przys[zł]o, [na], woyn[y], życ[z]y); 'Hetman' and 'że się' (letters left out) named in the header, not marked; no letter changed. The twelve clear/*.txt files got a header line saying they are the archive's clear copies and not the output of the key. Audit script for c024: 11 of 157 words depart. v2_score hole rate 0.063 before, 0.159 after; read_share not changed.

texts.summary: Postscript to the duplicate: Deboli will ask in every letter what Hetman Branicki is doing; the Prince of Nassau-Siegen writes that Branicki is one of the most devoted to Russia; Russia wants no new war.

reading_review.note: Read group by group against the key; groups whose value does not fit marked unread (reading/c024_1789-03-25.fix.tsv). The decode is unspaced syllables; word division and spelling are normalised in the English rendering, holes marked [...].

texts.summary: Potemkin has left for the army; talks with Nassau-Siegen on the rumoured Ukrainian rising, Branicki and the withdrawal of the Russian commissariats; Stackelberg's report that the King of Prussia offers Poland help; a charge that the King wanted Branicki poisoned; 'now is the time for Poland to rise'.
